elements_1962c: 2. Employed by or associated with an enterprise (distinct from the person)
3. Enterprise engaged in or affecting interstate commerce
4. Defendant conducted or participated in the conduct of the enterprise's affairs (Reves: operation-or-management)
5. Through a pattern of racketeering activity
6. Pattern: at least 2 predicate acts (§1961(1) list), related + continuous (H.J. Inc.)
7. Plaintiff injured in business or property by reason of the §1962 violation (Holmes: proximate cause)

civil_remedy_1964c.standing: Any person injured in their business or property
civil_remedy_1964c.sof_of_limitations: 4 years from discovery (Agency Holding Corp. v. Malley-Duff, 1987)
civil_remedy_1964c.securities_exclusion: Predicates that would be actionable as Exchange Act securities fraud are excluded (1996 RICO Reform)

interpretive.cite: Sedima, S.P.R.L. v. Imrex Co., 473 US 479 (1985)
interpretive.rule: No prior criminal conviction required; no racketeering injury required; §1964(c) available for any business/property injury from any RICO violation. Civil RICO is as broad as its text.

interpretive.cite: H.J. Inc. v. Northwestern Bell Telephone Co., 492 US 229 (1989)
interpretive.rule: Pattern = relatedness + continuity. Two acts necessary but not sufficient. Closed-ended (substantial period) or open-ended (ongoing threat) continuity. Resolves circuit split.
§1962(c) 'conduct or participate' requires operation-or-management role in directing the enterprise. Outside service providers who facilitate but do not direct are not §1962(c) defendants.
